It's not about seeing Brazil.
It's about reaching the Brazil that's hard to reach alone.

why this is harder than it looks

Brazil is enormous, and the best parts are the least connected

Nothing here is about you being unprepared. These places are genuinely difficult to organise from the outside, and that is the whole reason we exist.

The journey is the hard part

Getting from an international airport to somewhere like Atins takes a full day, more than one vehicle and at least one boat crossing. Along the way, almost nobody speaks English.

The park is far bigger than it looks

Lençóis Maranhenses covers more than 1,500 square kilometres and holds thousands of lagoons. Standard tours run to the same handful of them, at the same hour, with everyone else.

Planning eats your holiday

Days of searching, operators who answer only on WhatsApp and only in Portuguese, and prices you have no way of checking. That time was supposed to be the trip.

main destination

Lençóis Maranhenses

A desert that fills with rainwater once a year and turns into thousands of clear lagoons between white dunes. One of the most extraordinary landscapes in the world, and one of the least straightforward to reach.

We handle all of it: which airport to fly into, the road and river journey from São Luís, the 4x4 over the sand, where you stay in Barreirinhas, Atins or Santo Amaro, and a guide who takes you to lagoons the standard tours drive past.

How many days you actually need, when the water is at its highest, and what changes between four days and eight. It's all on the destination page.

for kitesurfers

The Wind Route

From Cumbuco to Atins, the northeast coast has steady wind from August to January, flat water lagoons and hundreds of kilometres you can ride in a single direction. It is one of the best kitesurf coastlines in the world, and one of the least organised.

If you're learning

We place you with a school that teaches properly, with gear included and lessons spread across days, at a spot with flat water and reliable wind.

If you already ride

We organise downwind runs between towns, with a support boat or vehicle following the coast, your luggage moved ahead, and a crew that knows the stretch.

Everything else, the transfers between towns, the rooms, the gear and the pick ups, is arranged before you land.

Where else we plan trips

We don't run the ground operation in these the way we do in the northeast. What we do is build the route and put you with the right people at each stop.

CaraívaBahia. No cars, no paved road, and a village that rewards staying longer than you planned.
The ChapadasDiamantina and Veadeiros. Waterfalls, canyons and trails that need a guide who reads the water.
Cangaço RouteThe backlands of Sergipe and Alagoas, and the history of the Brazilian outlaws, where it happened.
Gold RouteColonial Minas Gerais. Baroque towns, mountain roads and some of the best food in the country.
Carnival in OlindaPernambuco. The street carnival that is not the one on the postcards, with somewhere sensible to sleep.

Photographs of these come as we go back to each one. Every image on this site was taken by us, so nothing goes up until we have been there with a camera.

about us

Two people who travel the way we plan

Raiz is small on purpose. You deal with the same two people from the first message to the last day of your trip.

Yasminn

the northeast coast

Yasminn lived in the Lençóis Maranhenses. That is the difference between knowing a place and knowing how it works: which road floods, which boat leaves on time, which lagoon is worth the early start and which one everybody photographs.

She travels everywhere else the same way, staying long enough to learn how a place runs rather than how it photographs. Fifteen years of work travel across Brazil before Raiz, spent getting to know the bars, the restaurants and the kitchens of every city she landed in.

She designs the routes in the north and northeast, and she is the person answering your messages while you travel.

Elvis

the rest of Brazil

Elvis has travelled twenty four of Brazil's twenty seven states.

The chapadas, the sertão, the colonial towns, the carnival cities. He knows how they connect, which detours are worth the extra day, and where to eat once you arrive.

For five years he hosted travellers from all over the world in a spare room of his own flat in São Paulo, and showed them the city. That is where he learned what a visitor needs on the first day, usually before they think to ask.

questions

What people ask before they write to us

What exactly do you do?

We plan the trip and handle the logistics. That means the route, the transfers, the boats, the guides, the rooms and the reservations, plus a written itinerary and a direct line to us while you travel. We are not a tour operator selling fixed departures. Every route is built for the person taking it.

How much does it cost?

Our fee covers the planning and the coordination, and it depends on how many days and how many people. Everything on the ground you pay at local prices, with the full cost written down before anything is booked, so nothing is marked up on the way to you. Send us your dates and we will give you the number before you commit to anything.

Do I need to speak Portuguese?

No. We work in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. We brief every driver, guide and host before you arrive, and we are reachable on WhatsApp for the whole trip. Almost nobody in these places speaks English, and removing that barrier is most of what we do.

Couldn't I organise this myself?

In much of Brazil, yes, and we will tell you when that is the case. In the places we work, the roads need a 4x4 and local knowledge of the tides, the boats have no website, and the best places to eat and sleep are found by asking rather than by searching.

Is it safe, especially travelling alone as a woman?

It is the thing we screen for hardest. We work only with drivers, guides and hosts we have travelled with ourselves, and we end the relationship with anyone who treats a traveller without respect, however good the service is.

What happens if something goes wrong during the trip?

You message us. We answer in your language, and we know the people on the ground well enough to sort out a late boat, a closed road or a change of plan the same afternoon.

I already have an itinerary. Can you still help?

Yes. Send it over. We will tell you what we would change, what is too tight, and what you will probably regret skipping.
